title: Burst Capacity (Dedicated) — Customer interview working notes
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture raw notes from customer/prospect conversations re: Dedicated “burst capacity” option.
- Focus areas: (1) burst patterns (shapes + frequency), (2) acceptable degradation modes, (3) requested controls/guardrails (max TPS, concurrency, time windows), (4) what they want to see in metrics + billing.

Notes on anonymization
- Company names redacted in this doc; refer to them as DP-1/DP-2/etc. (Design Partner / Prospect).
- Regions referenced as customer-stated (us-east-1, eu-west-1, etc.)—some are “desired” not currently deployed.

High-level themes (across all calls)
- Baseline Dedicated sizing is typically set for weekday steady-state; bursts correlate with predictable events (batch jobs, weekly reports) or marketing launches.
- Customers do NOT want “best effort unlimited”; they want a contractable envelope + guardrails they can understand.
- Strong preference for strict admission control (deny/429/503) vs preempting other workloads.
- Customers repeatedly asked for “schedule windows” (time-of-day/day-of-week) so bursts can be allowed only during agreed timeboxes.
- Clear deny reasons and retry guidance are critical (avoid opaque 503s).

What customers mean by “burst” (common burst shapes)
1) Weekly batch/reporting spikes
- Common pattern: 1–4 hour burst, once a week (often Mon AM local time) or end-of-week reporting.
- Burst magnitude: 2x–8x baseline QPS/TPS.
- Often less sensitive to p95 latency; more sensitive to finishing the job by a deadline.

2) Daily diurnal peaks
- 2–3 hour peak window per day around business hours.
- Burst magnitude: 1.5x–3x baseline.
- Latency sensitivity: medium; they want interactive experiences to remain within SLA.

3) Launch / incident-driven spikes
- Unpredictable spikes: marketing email, push notification, partner integration rollouts.
- Burst magnitude: 5x–20x baseline (but short: 10–30 minutes).
- Strong emphasis on “we’d rather degrade gracefully than hard down.”

4) Customer-driven “backlog drain”
- They intentionally queue work and then drain when there’s a green window (e.g., “overnight job”).
- They’d like a way to say: allow burst up to X for Y minutes, then cool down.

Controls & guardrails requested (recurring asks)
A) Per-tenant hard caps (must-haves)
- “Max burst concurrency” (absolute number) — most requested control.
- “Max burst tokens/sec” or “max generated tokens/sec” — requested by teams thinking in throughput/cost terms.
- “Max burst requests/sec” — requested by teams thinking in API rate limiting.
- “Max burst compute share” expressed as “no more than N GPUs worth” (some customers asked for this but less common).

B) Time windows / schedules
- Allow burst only during specific windows:
  - Example: “Mon 08:00–12:00 local time” or “Daily 00:00–06:00 UTC”.
- Some want holidays/blackout days.
- Some want a “manual override” for exceptional events, gated by admin permission.

C) Cooldowns / backoff
- Many customers asked for:
  - a cooldown after heavy burst usage (prevents runaway cost + protects neighbors)
  - explicit “burst credits” per hour/day (even if not billed yet; they want predictability)

D) Per-region and per-model constraints
- “Only burst in region X” (data residency + latency).
- “Only burst for model family Y” (avoid quality inconsistencies).
- “Do not burst embeddings workload; ok to burst chat only” (one customer with mixed workloads).

E) Fallback preferences (when burst denied)
- Preference order varied:
  - Option 1: Deny fast with 429 + Retry-After (interactive apps want this)
  - Option 2: Route to smaller/cheaper model variant temporarily (batch jobs ok with this)
  - Option 3: Route to another region (often NOT acceptable due to residency)
- Strong ask: customer-configurable fallback policy (even if limited choices in v1).

F) Circuit breakers and “big red button”
- “We need a kill switch” (both customer-facing and internal) if behavior is unexpected.
- Want immediate disable without redeploying app config.

Acceptable degradation modes (what they’re willing to tolerate)
- Increased latency: commonly acceptable for batch; less so for interactive.
  - Many said: “p95 can double for a short window” if overall completion time improves.
- Denials/throttling: acceptable if explicit and predictable.
  - Customers asked for: clear 429 vs 503 semantics + reason code.
- Reduced quality: mixed acceptance.
  - Some are OK with fallback to smaller model for non-critical endpoints.
  - Others said: “no silent quality downgrade” (must be opt-in and observable).
- Partial feature degradation: e.g., disable tool-calling / structured outputs under stress.
  - Mentioned by one team but needs product discussion; not in initial scope.

Observability & transparency requested
- Real-time metrics they want in console/API:
  - burst admitted vs denied (count + rate)
  - current burst concurrency
  - burst tokens/sec (and baseline tokens/sec side-by-side)
  - time spent in burst state
  - top deny reasons (limit hit vs pool saturated vs policy window)
  - tail latency impact (p95/p99) during burst windows
- Post-event reporting:
  - “Show me the 2 hours where burst saved us” vs “where we got denied”
  - exportable logs/CSV for finance and incident review

Billing / pricing sensitivity (early, but consistent)
- Customers want to avoid paying for permanent overprovisioning.
- Most are OK with:
  - an add-on fee for “burst entitlement” + overage per usage unit (tokens or compute)
  - a pilot phase with shadow metering, as long as they can see what the bill WOULD have been.
- Finance teams ask for predictable ceilings:
  - “hard cap spend per day/week” or “hard cap burst tokens per month.”

Customer-by-customer notes

DP-1 (existing Dedicated; support escalation about throttling during predictable spikes)
- Workload: chat + summarization; strong weekday patterns.
- Regions: us-east-1 primary.
- Burst pattern:
  - weekly spike every Monday 09:00–11:00 ET, ~6x baseline requests.
  - sometimes ad hoc spikes when a partner launches a campaign.
- Current pain:
  - they can scale baseline, but don’t want to pay for idle GPUs 90% of week.
  - they see throttling / queue buildup; users experience timeouts.
- Requested controls:
  - max burst concurrency: “we want an explicit number we can set”
  - schedule windows: required (only allow burst during their defined spikes)
  - hard stop: if pool saturated, deny fast rather than slow death
- Acceptable degradation:
  - ok with 429 + Retry-After for a subset of endpoints; NOT ok with silent latency spikes > ~2x for interactive UI.
- Notes:
  - asked how they can test burst before enabling in prod (staging env + load test guidance).

DP-2 (design partner; batch analytics + nightly jobs)
- Workload: long-form generation + classification; mostly async/batch.
- Regions: eu-west-1 primary; strong data residency constraints.
- Burst pattern:
  - nightly runs, 00:00–04:00 UTC; 8x–10x baseline tokens/sec.
  - less frequent daytime interactive traffic.
- Requested controls:
  - max burst tokens/sec (preferred over req/sec; they budget by tokens)
  - per-model allowlist (only burst on Model A; no fallback to smaller model unless explicitly enabled)
  - prefer “credits” per night + cooldown if they burn through too fast
- Acceptable degradation:
  - ok with higher latency, ok with occasional denies if they can re-queue.
  - wants deterministic behavior (avoid flapping between admit/deny).
- Observability:
  - wants an “admission timeline” chart aligned to their job runs.

DP-3 (prospect evaluating Dedicated; interactive assistant)
- Workload: low latency chat, streaming, tool calling.
- Regions: us-west-2; may need multi-region later.
- Burst pattern:
  - diurnal peaks; launch spikes (push notifications).
  - short spikes: 10–20 min at 15x baseline.
- Requested controls:
  - max burst concurrency
  - “burst only for endpoint /v1/chat” (not for embeddings)
  - immediate fallback to smaller model acceptable ONLY if response includes a header / field indicating fallback occurred
- Acceptable degradation:
  - prefer fast denial with good retry guidance vs slow response.
- Open question from them:
  - “Is burst capacity truly isolated from hosted fleet? We don’t want hosted incidents to steal our burst.”
  - we answered: initial plan is controlled shared burst pools with strict limits; follow up with topology details.

DP-4 (existing Dedicated; multi-tenant SaaS on Redwood)
- Workload: mixed endpoints, many customer tenants behind their own gateway.
- Burst pattern:
  - end-of-month reporting, 2 days/month heavy usage.
- Requested controls:
  - “time windows” + “max daily burst” (cap) + alerts at 80% usage.
  - API to query current burst status so they can throttle upstream.
- Acceptable degradation:
  - ok with fallback model for non-premium SaaS tier.
  - wants ability to set per-route policy (premium customers get baseline only; free tier can burst).

Specific phrases worth reusing in PRD / docs
- “We want burst to be a seatbelt, not a turbo button.”
- “Don’t let burst become a noisy-neighbor problem with a new name.”
- “Tell me what happened: admitted/denied + why + what to do next.”

Open questions (for product/eng)
- Scheduling: do we support time windows in v1 config schema, or do we start with manual enable + planned window fields later?
- Deny semantics: 429 vs 503; do we vary by cause (tenant cap vs pool saturation)? Customers want consistency + actionable retry.
- Fallback: how to expose fallback safely without leaking infrastructure details (but still transparent)?
- Unit of limit: concurrency vs TPS vs tokens/sec — likely support more than one but need clear precedence/interaction.
- How to communicate “best effort” aspects without undermining trust (esp. when pool saturated)?

Action items (capture from interviews)
- Lauren + Mina: propose default deny semantics + headers/reason codes for v1 (tie to routing fallback doc).
- Sean (SRE): define minimum dashboards needed for pilot (admit/deny, saturation, neighbor p99 drift).
- Logan + Nadia: propose “shadow bill” report format and what fields customers can see in beta.
- Markus: identify 2–3 pilot candidates with predictable burst windows + willingness to accept deny behavior.

Appendix: Proposed control checklist (based on what customers asked for)
- [ ] burst_enabled (bool)
- [ ] max_burst_concurrency (int)
- [ ] max_burst_tokens_per_second (int)
- [ ] max_burst_requests_per_second (int)
- [ ] allowed_regions (list)
- [ ] allowed_models (list)
- [ ] schedule_windows (timezone + cron-like ranges)
- [ ] fallback_policy (deny_fast | fallback_model | fallback_region | none)
- [ ] cooldown_seconds (int)
- [ ] spend/usage caps (daily/weekly/monthly) — likely later; customers want it
- [ ] kill_switch (admin)

(End of working notes — not polished)
